title: Twilight pool tidy scratchpad
notes:
2026-03-10 / twilight shift notes (brain dump)

Quick context:
- Evening scaling wave at ~18:15 PT shifted load to pool-gpu-s-2; latency spikes for 4 short bursts (1-2m).
- Observed more idle inference sessions left open after model-switch rollouts (probable client SDK bug).
- Node 'rack-17-gpu-3' showing transient eth0 drops; flaps for ~30s at 18:22, recovered. SRE pinged.

Immediate to-do (order of attack):
1) Reclaim idle sessions older than 15m in pool-gpu-s-2. Use quick script, dry-run first.
   - dry run: ./scripts/session-reaper --pool pool-gpu-s-2 --older-than 15m --dry-run
   - live: ./scripts/session-reaper --pool pool-gpu-s-2 --older-than 15m --limit 50
   - Note: throttle to avoid thundering herd; sleep 1s between kills.

2) Validate warmup caches after reclaim. Check prefix cache hit ratio for the 128-token baseline.
   - query: curl -s https://ops-metrics.local/cache/pool-gpu-s-2 | jq '.prefix_hit_rate'
   - expected baseline: >= 0.72 at steady state; anything <0.6 -> investigate cache eviction policy.

3) Isolate node rack-17-gpu-3 if eth0 instability continues. Escalation path: cordon -> migrate pods -> replace NIC -> uncordon.
   - commands: kubectl cordon rack-17-gpu-3 && kubectl drain rack-17-gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
   - open ticket: INC-ops-2026-18 (if hardware team needs to replace NIC)

Housekeeping checklist (short):
- [ ] Add a small canary in front of warmup job to verify cache priming after reaper runs.
- [ ] Update incident template with "idle session refill" root cause options.
- [ ] Follow up with SDK team re: session close on model-switch (tag: @meera).

Observations / hypotheses (notes to self):
- Idle sessions appear correlated with model-switch rollouts where clients re-init but don't call close(); likely race in background heartbeat.
- Warmup cache eviction seems aggressive when queue depth > 120; probably eviction threshold set too low for this pool size.
- Network flap aligns with simultaneous k8s ephemeral IP churn during autoscaler downscale window — investigate autoscaler timing.

Small commands/snippets I keep returning to: 
- check pool utilization (last 15m): kubectl get hpa -n inference pool-gpu-s-2 -o yaml | grep -E "currentCPU|currentReplicas"
- identify stale sessions: SELECT session_id, last_seen, rps FROM sessions WHERE pool='pool-gpu-s-2' AND last_seen < now() - interval '15 minutes' ORDER BY last_seen ASC LIMIT 200; (psql on sessions-db)
- quick restart of reaper job if it dies: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/session-reaper

Edge cases to remember:
- Don't reclaim sessions if last_seen shows active KV-cache writes in last 30s — can be a long-running audio2text stream. Use conservative heuristics.
- If reaper crosses 500 kills in a minute, pause and notify on #infra-ops; too many kills may indicate upstream bug.

Meeting / followups:
- Sync with Meera tomorrow 10:30am PT to review SDK flush behavior (capture stack traces from client's heartbeat). Action: add debug logging to SDK client v0.4.2.
- Noah to schedule hw-fix inspection for rack-17 next maintenance window (weekend).

Questions I need to answer before sign-off:
- Is the warmup eviction threshold global or pool-scoped? (check infra-configs repo)
- Can we add a lightweight preflight on the canary routing layer to short-circuit cold starts?

Oddities / random reminders (personal):
- Bring headphones to late shift (remote debugging audio).
- Remind SRE to include NIC firmware version in hardware tickets.
- If I run the reaper live, leave a 30m rollback window and keep a watcher online (Meera/Noah).

Quick timeline for tonight if I run it: 19:00 - dry-run, 19:15 - live run (limit 50), 19:30 - verify cache hit rate, 20:00 - escalate if any node flapping persists.

Unresolved/parking-lot items:
- Follow up with product on whether model-switch telemetry should include explicit 'close' signal.
- Add a periodic job that runs lightweight cache-priming for top-50 prompts for each pool.

End of dump. Will tidy into a proper playbook if tonight's run is successful.
